newsitem.title: USA: Florida stuntman plans tightrope walk across Niagara.
newsitem.headline: Florida stuntman plans tightrope walk across Niagara.

text.p: Tightrope artist Jay Cochrane plans to become the first person in 100 years to walk across Niagara Falls on a wire.

But unlike acrobats such as the Great Blondin who made such crossings routine a century ago by traversing about 1,100 feet (335 metres) across the Horseshoe Falls, Cochrane plans to walk all the way from the New York side to the Ontario side -- about 3,500 feet (1,070 metres).
"By the time I get to a tower on the Canadian side, I'll have walked three times farther than anyone ever has at Niagara," he told Reuters on Tuesday at his home in Florida.
"I don't want people to worry about me dying. I won't. Oh, of course there's a chance, just like there's a chance you'll die when you get in a car, but this is what I do for a living," he said.
Last week the mayors of cities on either side of the falls gave their approval for the feat, which is scheduled to take place in September next year.
Cochrane, who says he in his mid-50's, strolled across the Yangtze River in 1995, a distance of 1098 feet (334 metres). He once sat on a wire for 21 days in Puerto Rico.
He said he would practice on a wire six feet (1.8 metres) above his backyard.
